title: The product frontend in the TripsSource design kit's look, its pages, words and behaviour unchanged
request: Update the UI without changing the content of DCLab, following the TripsSource design kit, its implementation guide and the example.
spec: Tripssource_UI/IMPLEMENTING.md (section 7: moving an existing product onto the kit) and TripsSource-Design-Kit.pdf
plan: Copy the kit unchanged into the frontend's sources, and the kit's two faces with their licences into fonts/.
Bridge: point the product's variables at the kit's tokens, so every screen takes the kit's colours, fonts and dark mode at once.
Draw the product's frame and shared components the kit's way in one file loaded after the kit, keeping every class, id and word.
Check against the PDF's measurements, in light and dark, at 375, 768, 1280 and 1600 px.

decisions.decision: Keep the product's markup and class names; restyle them with the kit's tokens instead of rewriting 19 views in ts- classes.
decisions.why: The content must not change, core.js and the browser test address the product's classes, and the guide's section 7 moves an existing product this way.

decisions.decision: Deep blue for actions and links, the light-green accent only as a marker (the current row's bar, the selected tab, focus, progress).
decisions.why: The kit's principle 4: one accent, used as a marker.

decisions.decision: The fonts are served by the app, copied from the TripsSource admin's committed files (google/fonts at 1edf95b, OFL).
decisions.why: The product names no other host (its CSP and its tests); nothing was downloaded.

decisions.decision: The kit's files go into app.css first, their comments left out.
decisions.why: A comment shows how to link a font host; the build's own test refuses any other host in the page.

change: dclab_rnd/agentic/web/src/kit/ (the kit, unchanged, with VERSION.md), fonts/ (Outfit, Plus Jakarta Sans), styles.css (variables on --ts-* tokens), look.css (the frame, sidebar, top bar, page header, tabs, panels, stat tiles, buttons, inputs, badges, tables, alerts, overlays), build.py (app.css from the kit, styles.css and look.css), core.js (the theme switch sets data-ts-theme too).

findings.defect: On a phone the page was squeezed into a narrow column.
findings.scenario: 375 px: the canvas was about 210 px wide.
findings.cause: look.css set the frame's two columns at every width, over the product's one-column rule below 960 px.
findings.fix: The columns stay with styles.css (its --side-w now the kit's sidebar width).
findings.test: the 19 pages at 375 px in the built-in browser: none scrolls sideways

findings.defect: The top bar's search and menu buttons shrank to slivers on narrow screens.
findings.scenario: 375 px: a blank pill and a 10 px menu button.
findings.cause: The kit's search keeps its padding while its text is hidden; flex items shrank.
findings.fix: Below 1100 px the search is the kit's round button; the top bar's buttons never shrink.

findings.defect: The Intern page scrolled 3 px sideways on a phone.
findings.scenario: A select in the page header, wider than the screen.
findings.cause: Its longest option plus the kit's wider input padding.
findings.fix: Header actions and selects are capped at their container's width.
findings.test: the 19 pages at 375, 768, 1280 and 1600 px: none scrolls sideways

findings.cause: The kit's header comment shows the Google Fonts link.
findings.fix: The kit's comments are left out of app.css; the files stay unchanged.

measurements.name: the kit's own checks (IMPLEMENTING.md section 6)
measurements.gate: page title Outfit 38 semibold; stat figure Outfit 32; md button 42 and header buttons 46; nav row 44 radius 14; panel radius 22 padding 20
measurements.result: page title Outfit 38 weight 600; figure 32; header buttons 46; nav row 44 radius 14; panel radius 22, padding 20; canvas radius 30; body Plus Jakarta Sans 13.5
limits: the browser test (make browser-test) was not run: Playwright's Chromium is not installed here

outcome: Every page of the product now has the TripsSource look in blue and light green, light and dark, with its words, routes and tests unchanged.
lessons: Restyle an existing product through its own class names and a token bridge: every page changes at once and nothing that addresses the markup breaks.
Check every width the kit names; a rule written for the wide frame broke the phone layout.
risks: A few product-only pieces (charts' series colours, the blueprint layer, syntax colours) keep their own colours.
